concepts.definition: Revision of the Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set (IACS), including carrier addition, removal, merger and splitting; the set is not numerically frozen.

grounding.quote:
The IACS is not numerically frozen. Adding, removing, merging, or splitting a
carrier is lawful through accepted Ontology and design re-entry. For every such
revision, accepted design:

concepts.label: IACS revision

concepts.definition: The Promotion Test distinguishes independently justified architectural types from Subordinate Payloads that remain nested, private or local to a carrier family.

grounding.quote:
A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum, or named schema record must
justify its existence as an architectural boundary, not merely as payload
detail.

concepts.label: Promotion Test

concepts.definition: Boundary Inflation is design debt: typing difficulty promotes payload details to peers, internal records become public without a new authoritative boundary, near-identical top-level types multiply where one carrier family suffices, or one migration silently becomes parallel schema migrations.

grounding.quote: Boundary Inflation is design debt, not progress.

concepts.label: Boundary Inflation

conditions: A realization derives from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.
concepts.definition: Reference-derived module design establishes the target boundary through an auditable constitutional-WHAT-to-reference-to-target derivation, preventing incidental reference drift, delivery quirks, helper sprawl and authority paths from becoming target design.

grounding.quote:
When a realization is being derived from an existing design line, released
tenant, or reference implementation, design-method completion must not rest on
code comparison alone.

concepts.label: Reference-derived module design

concepts.definition: The three-view design asset comprises a classDiagram domain model, sequenceDiagram execution model and stateDiagram-v2 lifecycle model. These are fidelity-checked projections of accepted Ontology and jointly the sign-off surface for identity, authority, behavior, lifecycle and axiom conformance.

grounding.quote:
The views are not decorative and they are not peer truth surfaces. They are
fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology. Together they are the
sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behavior, lifecycle, and axiom
conformance.

concepts.label: Ontology and three-view design asset

concepts.definition: Ontology evidence is the accepted semantic basis cited for the active boundary, either a full accepted Ontology or a parent-derived boundary-bounded slice.

grounding.quote:
The design asset must cite one accepted Ontology for the active boundary and
include or reference its:

concepts.label: Accepted Ontology evidence

concepts.definition: Invariant reconstruction sufficiency is a property of the existing Ontology, authority/admission relation, frame declaration, views and module mapping for a declared action and causally closed affected set. Its action/relation classifications are preserves, changes, duplicates and violates; these are not evaluation verdicts.

grounding.quote:
The evidence must recover every governing relation in the action's causally
closed affected set and distinguish the following action classifications.
These describe the action/relation pair; they are not evaluation verdicts.

concepts.label: Invariant Reconstruction Sufficiency

concepts.definition: The classDiagram is the structural domain projection of Ontology. Its standard stereotypes are <<prime-conformant>>, <<subordinate>>, <<effect-edge>>, <<deferred>>, <<authoritative>> and <<downstream>>; '+' means public/exported and '-' means module-local/private.

grounding.quote:
The `classDiagram` is the structural domain projection of the Ontology. It must
show, for the active boundary:

concepts.label: Domain model

concepts.definition: The sequenceDiagram is the behavioral projection of Ontology functions and authority, showing supported execution from admitted input to result or truthful stop.

grounding.quote:
The `sequenceDiagram` is the behavioral projection of Ontology functions and
authority. It must show the supported execution path from admitted input to
result or truthful stop. It must name the owner and required authority of every
decision, admission, execution, projection, and effect boundary.

concepts.label: Sequence model

concepts.definition: The stateDiagram-v2 is the lifecycle projection of Ontology entities, covering the active boundary's complete admitted lifecycle.

grounding.quote:
The `stateDiagram-v2` is the lifecycle projection of Ontology entities. It must
show the complete admitted lifecycle for the active boundary, including
refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation, and terminal states that the
boundary can produce. Every transition must bind to an Ontology function and
name its owning authority, admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection,
or external act.

concepts.label: State model

concepts.definition: Cross-view axiom evaluation evaluates applicable product, graph, language, runtime, handler and module axioms on a named design boundary and governing basis, keeping applicability distinct from conformance.

grounding.quote:
The design pack evaluates every applicable product, graph, language, runtime,
handler and module axiom using the shared
[result algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra). Applicability and conformance
are separate predicates on the named design boundary and governing basis.

concepts.label: Cross-view axiom evaluation

concepts.definition: The design gate separates conformance assessment from the design authority's accepted/non-accepted decision. Retrospective implementation is evidence to be evaluated against prior authority, not an independent author of semantic truth.

grounding.quote:
design-conformance predicate. The design authority separately records its
`accepted` or `non-accepted` decision. An acceptance decision requires the
satisfied conformance result and the authority's lawful mandate; non-acceptance
retains the actual failed, unresolved or diagnosed conformance result and does
not itself mean falsified.

concepts.label: Design gate and retrospective work

conditions: A material semantic boundary is being designed.
concepts.definition: Computational realization projection exposes abstract data types, identity/key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation/effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings that domain views alone can conceal. Every material component has explicit semantic and operational roles; its declared role set is design authority.

grounding.quote:
**The projection.** At a material semantic boundary, the design must project
the domain design into its computational realization: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and effect
boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational mappings. The
cross-view evaluation extends to prove the domain views and this projection
describe one system.

concepts.label: Computational Realization Projection

concepts.definition: Optional theoretical framing treats the Markov object as a candidate stable, self-bounding identity-bearing cut. IACS is an engineering analogue of the smallest such cut; Promotion tests independent boundary authority; inflation mistakes fragments for peer objects; strong semantic-boundary typing prevents fuzzy or controller-owned identity.

grounding.quote:
`WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md` treats a Markov object as a candidate
identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern whose effective blanket
separates what is load-bearing for identity from what is load-bearing for
context. Under that framing, the engineering problem is not "how do I name more
field groups?" but "what is the smallest lawful boundary that preserves the
thing's identity under variation?"

concepts.label: Theoretical framing for boundary law

conditions: The method governs a realization boundary.
concepts.definition: Recommended module roles: Carrier defines typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts, transitions, records or envelopes; Semantic kernel transforms carriers without side effects; Effect shell performs emissions, publication, network/subprocess/persistence/operator delivery; Projection derives read models/reports from authoritative truth; Binding/adapter converts external boundaries to internal carriers without inventing law; Constructor/materialization writes artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. Modules bound graph-traversal reasoning and expose recurrence.

grounding.quote:
When this method governs a realization boundary, modules should be classified by
role.

Recommended roles are:

concepts.label: Design module taxonomy

concepts.definition: The canonical evidence route is constitutional WHAT/requirements → Ontology, IACS, target design and three-view evidence → implementation/module-derived tests → reconciliation/acceptance → promotion/closure. The reverse feedback route supplies evidence, counterexamples or falsification to affected Ontology/design relations without selecting or accepting their semantics.

grounding.quote:
The first chain is semantic derivation. The second is evidence feedback and
cannot select or accept the affected semantic answer. When
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, the two chains may proceed together without
making implementation semantic authority. Design still owns the structural
`HOW`.

concepts.label: Design-to-module evidence route

concepts.definition: Module-derived Unit Tests are module-owned proof lanes within urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance. DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD owns that concept and proof relation, not Product UAT or acceptance. Integration, scenario and sandbox lanes remain downstream proof families.

grounding.quote:
This clause consumes the product-assurance bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance` declared by
`SPEC_METHOD.md#testing-strategy-taxonomy`. `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` owns the
module-derived `Unit Test` concept and proof relation inside that context; it
does not take ownership of Product-level UAT or acceptance meaning.

Unit tests under this method are module-owned proof lanes.

concepts.label: Module-derived Unit Tests

concepts.definition: Module lifecycle confirmation detects ambiguity about intended operational use at every designed module, function, application/runtime/plugin/public-interface/data surface, graph function or GTL module. It consumes the Spec operational lifecycle chain and is neither a release plan nor a replacement for RELEASE_METHOD.

grounding.quote:
The canonical operational lifecycle chain is defined by `SPEC_METHOD.md` under
the Operational Lifecycle Sufficiency Rule. This method consumes that canonical
chain; it does not redefine the phases.

This checklist is not a release plan and does not replace `RELEASE_METHOD.md`.
It is an ambiguity detector for ultimate intended use.

concepts.label: Module lifecycle confirmation

concepts.definition: Typed immutable carriers are the preferred source-truth representation: constructors/parsers produce carriers, transforms return another carrier or a closed result, and projections read without mutation.
exceptions: Mutation may be materially necessary.

grounding.quote:
Preferred shape:

- constructor or parser produces a typed carrier
- transforms consume one carrier and return another carrier or a closed result
- projections read those carriers without mutating them

concepts.label: Immutable carriers

concepts.definition: Semantic-function totality is a preference bounded by language and problem, with an admitted input domain, intended result and explicit continuation, repair, recovery, re-entry, refusal, yielding or termination. Method-boundary returns retain the core record and original domain outcome.

grounding.quote:
Semantic functions should be total, or as close as the language and problem
allow. Bind their admitted input domain, intended result and permitted
continuation, repair, recovery, re-entry, refusal, yielding or termination under
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) and
[bounded construction](FOUNDATIONS.md#bounded-construction). The method-boundary
return uses the core result record with the original domain outcome.

concepts.label: Semantic-function totality

concepts.definition: Effect edges include file writes, network calls, subprocesses, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and database mutation. Preferred flow admits authoritative input, produces a typed plan/outcome, applies effects at the edge and publishes downstream events/projections.

grounding.quote:
The preferred sequence is:

1. admit or parse the authoritative input
2. transform it into a typed plan or outcome
3. apply effects at the edge using that plan or outcome
4. publish resulting events or projections downstream

concepts.label: Effect edges

concepts.definition: An undeclared semantic center is a controller, manager, service, loop or public wrapper that reconstructs closure, identity, failure, next work or current truth through orchestration, legacy fallback, payload fragments or open dictionaries.

grounding.quote:
A wrapper that decides them through procedural orchestration, legacy fallbacks,
payload-fragment reconstruction or open-dictionary handling becomes an
undeclared semantic center and fails the authority/preservation conditions.

concepts.label: Undeclared semantic center

concepts.definition: Coupling concerns dependency shape and the number of places that can invent meaning. Excessive coupling includes shared mutation by many modules, projections inferring truth from implementation state, consumers rebuilding source truth from raw artifacts, and tests depending on duplicated meaning.

grounding.quote:
Reducing coupling means reducing the number of places where meaning can be
invented.

concepts.label: Coupling

concepts.definition: Governance surfaces describe state, preserved structure, unresolved IDs/pressure, route eligibility, lawful edit/proof frontier, admitted policy identity and continuity. Strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor works. Bound responsibility and actual operation/decision grants are instance premises.

grounding.quote:
- governance surfaces describe the state, boundary, and admissible routes
- strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should do the work

concepts.label: Governance and strategy separation

conditions: A realization boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation.
concepts.definition: Opportunistic optimization improves the active area while remaining subordinate to constitutional truth, declared ownership evidence and functional equivalence. Cross-boundary opportunities are repricing inputs rather than automatically admitted work.

grounding.quote:
When a realization boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor, or
bounded implementation work, the area should be left better than it was found.

This does not outrank constitutional truth, declared module ownership evidence,
or functional equivalence. It is subordinate to them.

concepts.label: Opportunistic optimization

concepts.definition: Recurrence extraction reviews repeated realization patterns as commonization candidates. Typical, not mandatory, properties are non-Product truth, authority neutrality, reuse across at least two tickets/boundaries and local-adapter consumption without ownership changes. Examples include expectation derivation, contract/policy carriers, proof fixtures, effect plans and non-semantic constructor helpers.

grounding.quote:
When the same realization pattern appears across more than one processed
boundary, review must treat that pattern as a commonization candidate rather
than as another purely local cleanup.

concepts.label: Recurrence extraction

conditions: A ticket adopts the method and claims its boundary has been processed.
concepts.definition: Post-ticket design review checks the exact closure claim and its causally closed selected function against accepted design, rather than the whole Product/history or only previous findings. Ticket status, reopening, dependencies and follow-up recording remain TICKET_METHOD responsibilities.

grounding.quote:
`TICKET_METHOD.md` remains the authority for ticket status, closure mechanics,
reopening, dependency handling, and follow-up ticket recording. This rule states
what the design check must cover when this method governs the ticketed
boundary.

concepts.label: Post-ticket design review

conditions: A crossing occurs between interface families.
concepts.definition: Semantic interface non-bleed preserves each family's authoritative source and downstream consumption. Projection-to-closure, report/prompt-to-admission, wrapper-to-kernel and adapter-to-semantic-owner changes are undeclared authority transfers.

grounding.quote:
consume it. Projection-to-closure, report/prompt-to-admission,
wrapper-to-kernel and adapter-to-semantic-owner changes are undeclared authority
transfers, not ordinary interface translation. This is semantic non-bleed;
smaller functions alone do not establish it.

concepts.label: Interface bleed

concepts.definition: A proxy interface is a new-looking surface forwarding to old authority, reconstructing missing truth from the old path, retaining that path behind a new name, or keeping proofs green while old law governs. It is bridge debt.

grounding.quote:
A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that:

- forwards to the old authority path
- reconstructs missing truth from the old path
- keeps the old path executable behind a new name
- allows proofs to stay green while the old law still governs

This is bridge debt, not progress.

concepts.label: Proxy interface

concepts.definition: Design Review Questions is an owner-route index selecting decision evidence for the exact adopted boundary and claim, not a second definition of the decisions.

grounding.quote:
Review the exact adopted boundary and claim by applying
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application).
Acquire the applicable owners below with the actual design and implementation.
The table selects the required decision evidence; it is not another definition
of those decisions.

concepts.label: Design review owner routes

conditions: A claim concerns functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner truth or low coupling.
concepts.definition: Functional realization review applies section 4 policies and section 14 owner routes to modules, carriers and data entities in any language, using the exact boundary's Ontology, atom/IACS mapping, views, computational binding, implementation and module proof.

grounding.quote:
A claim of functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner
truth or low coupling selects the [section 4 policies](#4-functional-bias-without-language-mandate) and section 14 owner routes for its
exact boundary. Evaluate them against the admitted Ontology, atom/IACS mapping,
three views, computational binding, implementation and module-owned proof.
The check applies in any language to modules, carriers and data entities.

concepts.label: Functional realization review

concepts.definition: Method adoption may occur through ADR/design citation, naming the preferred discipline in AGENTS.md, migration-ticket review criteria or module-role classification; adoption can be partial and boundary-scoped.

grounding.quote:
Projects may adopt this method by:

- citing it in ADRs or design surfaces
- naming it in `AGENTS.md` as the preferred realization discipline
- using it as review criteria for implementation-migration tickets
- classifying implementation modules by the taxonomy in this method

concepts.label: Design method adoption

concepts.definition: Method ownership allocation: SPEC_METHOD owns constitutional process, authority flow, repricing and migration; RELEASE_METHOD owns release-cut, Product, install, qualification, exact-cut acceptance and selector/version-line promotion; ODD_METHOD owns graph-native constructive shape and operative unit; DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD owns preferred implementation/module structure; UX_METHOD conditionally refines UI rendering, state transitions and effect membranes.

grounding.quote:
- `SPEC_METHOD.md` governs constitutional process, authority flow, repricing,
  and migration law
- `RELEASE_METHOD.md` governs release-cut, Product, install, qualification, and
  version-line promotion evaluation
- `ODD_METHOD.md` governs graph-native constructive carrier law
- `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` governs preferred realization structure inside
  implementation and design modules
- `UX_METHOD.md` refines this method for UX surfaces with rendering,
  state-transition, and effect-membrane rules; load it only when the work
  realizes a UX surface

concepts.label: Related method ownership

concepts.definition: The method's implementation discipline requires readability, modularity and explicit locations of meaning and effects without mandating a language, elimination of imperative code, categorical vocabulary or replacement of every exception by a custom algebraic type.

grounding.quote:
This method does not require:

- one specific programming language
- elimination of all imperative code
- monadic or category-theory vocabulary
- replacing every exception with a custom algebraic type

It does require that the implementation shape remain readable, modular, and
honest about where meaning lives and where effects happen.

concepts.label: Design discipline scope and non-goals

concepts.definition: STDO Foundations declares commitments and premises for purposeful construction by finite-resource actors. The core owns shared result, current-state, bounded-work, authority-conservation, independent-assessment and construction-assurance decisions; particular methods bind domain types, predicates, policies and authority.

grounding.quote:
The core owns the shared decisions about results, current state, bounded work,
authority conservation, required independent assessment and construction assurance. Particular methods supply domain predicates, types,
policies and authority bindings. They apply those decisions without maintaining
parallel rules. A specialization does not assign unrelated software or calculus
definitions a common purpose, signature or workflow.

concepts.label: STDO Foundations

concepts.definition: The foundations context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:foundations, owned by the STDO Specification Methodology Product authority. U_foundation supplies adequacy and reserved value choices; O_subject supplies scoped identity, boundary, state and material relations; kappa_interpretation supplies consumer meaning; Sigma_contract supplies obligations and variation. Operation and decision authority remain separate source-owned relations.

grounding.quote:
A selected purpose U_foundation supplies an adequacy predicate and reserved value choices.
An object O_subject supplies a scoped identity, boundary, current state and material
relations. An interpretation context kappa_interpretation determines the meaning available to
a consumer. A governing specification Sigma_contract declares obligations and admissible
variation. For an evaluation performing operations, the imported operation authority bounds
its permitted effects. Other operations retain the grants of their owning
contracts. Decision authority bounds disposition. These remain distinct
source-owned relations. Observations and arguments
support claims only on their declared subject and basis.

concepts.label: Foundational premises and standing

concepts.definition: F1 adopts purpose and owner-selected adequacy/value choices; F2 interprets supported claims on a subject/basis; F3 distinguishes scoped identity, persistent current state, representation and history; F4 conserves outer-contract relations under compatibility/loss without merging owners; F5 admits truthful unknown, inadequate and interrupted handling under finite capacity; F6 separates evidence from owner-bound operation/decision authority.

grounding.quote:
| F5 Finite capacity and total handling | Actor resources are finite; the selected control domain admits truthful handling of unknown, inadequate and interrupted conditions. | Total handling is not omniscience, universal idempotence or guaranteed solution. |
| F6 Evidence and authority | Evidence supports claims; operation and decision authority come from their bound owners. | A judgment or available tool is not permission. |

concepts.label: Foundational commitments F1–F6

concepts.definition: Representation is encoding; interpretation relates encoding to meaning in a declared context. Equal encodings can differ in meaning and different encodings can share scoped meaning.

grounding.quote:
A representation is an encoding. An interpretation relates that encoding to
meaning under a declared context. Equal encodings can have different meanings;
different encodings can represent the same scoped meaning. A parser, structural
validator or successful join does not establish interpretation fidelity.

concepts.label: Interpretation and representation

concepts.definition: An interface exists to acquire, convey, judge or effect a material relation needed by a transformation. Its obligations derive from that relation and the outer contract; the purpose owner fixes observable adequacy.

grounding.quote:
owns justification of method burden. The purpose owner fixes the observable adequate outcome. An interface exists
because a transformation needs to acquire, convey, judge or effect a material
relation. Its obligations derive from that relation and the outer contract.
A convenient signature, existing function or local test cannot invent Product
meaning. Within UP-014's scope, the method owner justifies material method burden.
This does not add a purpose dependency to calculus definitions or constraints.

concepts.label: Purpose and interfaces

concepts.definition: Identity distinguishes a scoped object; work state is the current subject under construction; events, assessments and receipts are scoped observation/judgment evidence; acceptance is an owner decision. These are distinct.

grounding.quote:
Work state is the current subject under construction. An event, assessment or
receipt is evidence of a scoped observation or judgment. Acceptance is an owner
decision. None of these substitutes for another. Historical evidence remains
historical when current premises change. Reuse follows
[Change impact and evidence retention](#change-impact-and-evidence-retention),
using the current subject acquired under [Workspace and context](#workspace-and-context).

concepts.label: Identity, state and evidence

concepts.definition: Reference-only imports from urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation preserve owner-qualified meanings: frame-set authority is the human declaring/accepting project frames; semantic authority owns a material relation's meaning; evaluation authority may evaluate; operation authority is an owner grant to construct/transform/admit/publish/mutate during evaluation; decision authority may dispose a result; actor identity names the human, agent, tool or process doing work.

grounding.quote:
Source and target meanings are identical owner-qualified references, not new
local definitions. Direction is from the named source to this foundational
context; loss is none and no translation or ownership transfer is asserted.

concepts.label: Reference-only authority imports

concepts.definition: Typed composition conserves material outer-contract meaning and original producer coordinates across compatible relations, including failures, citations, uncovered coverage and uncertainty. Shared machinery does not merge semantic ownership, responsibility or independence.

grounding.quote:
Relations compose only when their source and destination types, interpretation,
identity, lifecycle, preconditions, authority and effects are compatible. A
handoff conserves the material outer contract and original producer coordinates.
It retains known failures and their citations, required uncovered coverage and
uncertainty. Local success cannot erase a failed or missing material relation.

concepts.label: Typed composition and conservation

concepts.definition: Finite-capacity handling binds the actor and capability envelope material to an activation's claim; sufficiency, bounded work and resumption retain their owning contracts rather than introducing universal budgets, ledgers or measurement gates.

grounding.quote:
The [frame laws](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#reference-frame-laws) own material
sufficiency and capability; the [totality rule](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#8-totality-rule)
owns closed design handling. Each activation binds the actor and capability
envelope materially needed by its claim. No universal numeric budget, resource
ledger or measurement gate follows.

concepts.label: Finite capacity and total handling

concepts.definition: Judgment binds a predicate, exact subject, basis, evidence, assessor and required independence. Definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted claims have distinct standing; production, assessment and disposition are separate responsibilities. Meaning, evaluation, operation and decision authority remain distinct even in one actor.

grounding.quote:
Definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted
claims have distinct standing. A judgment binds a predicate, exact subject,
basis, evidence, assessor and any required independence. Producing a candidate,
assessing it and disposing it are separate responsibilities. Evidence establishes
only its supported claim; it cannot supply an operation or decision mandate.
The [Dispose contract](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#dispose) applies the bound
decision authority to its permitted dispositions.

concepts.label: Judgment and authority

conditions: The governing contract selects independent assessment and its claim-relative conditions.
concepts.definition: Independent assessment is distinct from author self-review, structural disjointness, procedural independence and shared-cause analysis. Its required authorship, evidence, reference-exposure, actor and configuration conditions come from the governing contract.

grounding.quote:
The governing contract selects whether independent assessment is required and
which authorship, evidence, reference-exposure, actor or configuration conditions
apply to the claim. Where nonauthor assessment is required, its assessor is not
an author of the reviewed subject or repair. Self-review remains authoring
evidence; a human acceptance decision cannot turn it into independent
assessment.

concepts.label: Independent assessment

concepts.definition: Algorithmic, informational and computational accounts simultaneously describe the selected transformation, preserved interpreted distinctions and concrete execution through machines, people or mixed processes with material effects/costs. A, I and C_H denote proposed accounts, not established categories merely by naming.

grounding.quote:
Keep three accounts distinct. An algorithmic account specifies the selected
transformation. An informational account explains interpreted distinctions and
their preservation. A computational account realises the operation through a concrete execution
environment: software and hardware, people and communication, or a mixed
process, with the effects and resource costs material to its obligations. They are
simultaneous descriptions, not successive SDLC stages.

concepts.label: Orthogonal descriptions

concepts.definition: Bind, Acquire, Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose are Transformation Library contract-vocabulary operations with conditional obligations specialized by domain types, predicates and authority; they are not six compulsory stages or runtime APIs.

grounding.quote:
The [transformation library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md) describes Bind, Acquire,
Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose. The library defines a shared contract vocabulary with conditional obligations
for this selected method domain. Particular methods specialize it through their
own types, predicates and authority; it is not six compulsory stages or six
runtime APIs. No operation authority follows from a contract definition.
A changed detailed determination still returns to its owning contract.

concepts.label: Canonical contract operations

concepts.definition: Construction activation consumes an exact subject and sufficient projected reference frame with acquisition paths, declared fidelity and scope. Independent evaluation may need overlapping context at different capability or evidence altitude.

grounding.quote:
The corpus may exceed one actor's capacity. An activation consumes a sufficient
projected reference frame and exact subject, with acquisition paths for required
material. The projection has declared fidelity and scope; it is not a rival
source of authority. Independent evaluation may require overlapping context at
a different capability or evidence altitude.

concepts.label: Construction and use

concepts.definition: A core result is a semantic contract about one predicate on one exact subject/basis, retaining verdict, performance, original qualified domain outcome, evidence/citations, unresolved obligations and material effect observations. Verdicts are exactly satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis; performance is performed, not_performed or unconfirmed; effects are not_requested, not_started, completed, partial, reverted or unknown. These coordinates answer distinct questions.

grounding.quote:
A result makes a claim about one predicate on one subject and basis. Its core
record contains the predicate, exact subject and basis, verdict, performance,
original qualified domain outcome, supporting evidence and citations, unresolved
obligations and material effect observations. A reference can carry these when
its resolution preserves their meaning and availability. This is a semantic
contract, not a mandatory serialization format or additional work carrier.

concepts.label: Core result algebra

concepts.definition: Result conjunction evaluates all required predicates and material joins on a declared composite subject/basis. Its result retains authenticated contributions, predicate mappings, failures/citations, uncovered coverage, uncertain effects and invalidators; a summary does not replace components.

grounding.quote:
Conjunction evaluates whether all required predicates and their material joins
hold on the declared composite subject and basis. It retains the contributing
results, their authentication and predicate mapping, known failures and their
citations, uncovered required coverage, uncertain effects and invalidators.
The aggregate is another result in the same algebra, with those components
available through sufficient references. Its summary never replaces them.

concepts.label: Result conjunction

concepts.definition: Construction assurance binds obligation, interpreted predicate, subject, basis, assumptions and admissible evidence, applying preservation at joins, assertion/observation justification at evaluation, dependence/risk at evidence selection and applicability at change/reuse.

grounding.quote:
An assurance consumer binds the selected obligation, interpreted predicate,
subject, governing basis, assumptions and admissible evidence. Apply the
subrelations below at the decision that relies on them: preservation at a
construction join, assertion and observation justification at evaluation,
dependence and risk at evidence selection, and applicability at change or reuse.
The consumer supplies its domain policy and required assurance; these shared
relations create no additional evaluation stage, role, record or authority.
Every conclusion uses the [result algebra](#result-algebra), and required
predicates combine under [result conjunction](#result-conjunction).

concepts.label: Construction assurance

concepts.definition: Preservation for construction A toward Z binds assumptions Gamma, state/trace domains X_i, transitions F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1), and properties P_i. Every admitted step must satisfy: for all x,x', P_i(x) and F_i(x,x') imply P_(i+1)(x'). Material effects and trace properties belong to the outcome predicate.

grounding.quote:
For every x and x':
  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x') implies P_(i+1)(x').

concepts.label: Preservation obligations

concepts.definition: For obligation r, Q_r = interpret(r, Gamma, Omega) is its required predicate over cases containing material inputs, behavior and environment. Assertions target q_t; pi: Omega → O models observations and T ⊆ O × R is the admitted checker relation into core results. sat/fal abbreviate verdicts about q_t, not execution states.

grounding.quote:
For an owning obligation r, let Q_r = interpret(r, Gamma, Omega) be its required
predicate over a declared case domain Omega. A case includes material inputs,
behaviour and environment. Justify this interpretation with its conditions,
exceptions and permitted alternatives. A source identifier or digest establishes
which text was selected, not that Q_r expresses it faithfully.

concepts.label: Assertions and observations

concepts.definition: Assertion provenance records obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies supporting an expected predicate. Execution provenance records the actual checker, exact subject, environment, inputs, acquired observations and result. Construction and assertion paths may refine a shared obligation differently without automatically covering one another.

grounding.quote:
Assertion provenance identifies the owning obligation, interpretation,
assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies that justify the expected
predicate. Execution provenance identifies the actual checker, exact subject,
applicable environment, inputs, acquired observations and result. Preserve both
relations in existing bindings and evidence; execution logs cannot justify an
expected answer's derivation. A shared derivation can serve a declared family
without a separate document for every test.

concepts.label: Parallel assurance and provenance

concepts.definition: Assurance selection is made by the actor with admitted work authority for required obligations, material failure consequences and resource limits. Quantified assurance is conditional on a declared population/uncertainty model, priors, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits.

grounding.quote:
The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects assurance for the
required obligations, material failure consequences and resource limits. Bind
coverage, uncertainty and the conditions for action or acceptance. More evidence
strengthens a claim only within its applicability and dependence account;
test counts or an assumed preference for more checks supply neither. Required
safety, authority and acceptance conditions remain applicable to every selected
strategy.

concepts.label: Risk and assurance selection

conditions: Any carrier addition, removal, merge or split is proposed.

grounding.quote:
- re-derives the complete IACS and classifies every addition, removal, merge,
  and split;
- reruns the Promotion Test and Boundary Inflation prohibition over the full
  revised set, not only newly introduced carriers;
- updates every conformance or checker subject to the declared composite
  carrier relation under `SPEC_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-022`; and
- reconciles implementation to the revised set before promotion or closure.

This obligation consumes the federal assurance law without restating it. A
prohibition without a lawful revision path is false. A revision is also false
if its gates inspect only new carriers, its assurance surfaces retain a weaker
or obsolete subject, or implementation is not reconciled before closure.

constraints.statement: Lawful revision requires accepted Ontology and design re-entry, re-derivation of the complete set with every change classified, Promotion and Boundary Inflation checks over the entire revised set, every conformance/checker subject updated to the declared composite carrier relation under UP-022, and implementation reconciliation before promotion or closure. The source calls a prohibition without lawful revision false; it also calls revisions false when gates inspect only new carriers, assurance retains weaker/obsolete subjects, or implementation remains unreconciled at closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced federal assurance law and UP-022 are not supplied.

conditions: A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record is proposed.

grounding.quote:
The burden of proof is on promotion.

Designers and reviewers should assume a candidate type stays subordinate until
an irreducible boundary is shown.

constraints.statement: A top-level type must justify an architectural boundary. Subordinate Payload promotion requires at least one of: authoritative source carrier; public/persisted contract boundary; directly pattern-matched explicit public-outcome variant; reuse across multiple modules without semantic bleed; independent versioning, publication or admission. Mere internal record detail, once-used field grouping, open-dict typing shim, private variation never crossing a true interface, or cosmetic/local mirror is insufficient. A shape needing no independent authority, independent reuse or direct pattern matching remains subordinate and nested/private/local. Proof rests on promotion; reviewers should assume subordination until an irreducible boundary is shown.

conditions: Schema work is undertaken; the wide-family distinction additionally applies when a schema or ticket lists a wide family of types.

grounding.quote:
If a schema or ticket lists a wide family of types, it must distinguish:

- the Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set
- Subordinate Payloads

Failing to make that distinction is design drift.

Typed closure does not excuse Boundary Inflation.

constraints.statement: Schema work must declare IACS, authoritative types, downstream projections, subordinate shapes and payloads intentionally deferred from promotion. Wide type families must distinguish IACS from Subordinate Payloads; failure is design drift. Typed closure does not excuse Boundary Inflation.

conditions: Reference-derived realization.

grounding.quote:
If a target realization cannot show that derivation chain, it is not yet
design-method complete under this method.

constraints.statement: Completion cannot rest on code comparison. Required ordered evidence is constitutional WHAT, reference design, target Ontology with reference mapping, target design mapping, target module-boundary assets and implementation. Minimum assets name source reference surfaces; accepted target Ontology dispositions for reference entities, functions, lifecycle, authority, effects and projections; replacing/binding target surfaces; explicit preserved/reshaped/deferred/delivery-demoted mapping; and method-required boundary assets including Ontology-derived IACS and three-view design. Without this derivation the target is not yet design-method complete.

conditions: Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary.
exceptions: Unchanged boundaries cite their accepted basis; local realization work without a material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate the gate.

grounding.quote:
Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary must carry
one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset before
the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure. When
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, design evidence, implementation, and tests
may develop together before that gate. Otherwise the affected unresolved,
contradictory, or materially non-equivalent relation is accepted before
retained implementation establishes it. Unchanged boundaries cite their
accepted basis; local realization work with no material semantic-boundary delta
does not recreate this gate.

constraints.statement: Before promotion or closure the boundary must carry one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view asset containing all three distinct domain, execution and lifecycle views. When co_evolution_admissible(B) holds, evidence, implementation and tests may develop together before the gate; otherwise an affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation must be accepted before retained implementation establishes it.
constraints.uncertainty: The definition of co_evolution_admissible(B) lies outside the supplied sections.

conditions: A design asset concerns an active boundary.
exceptions: Governing composition and effect algebra is required where applicable.

grounding.quote:
The Ontology may be a boundary-bounded slice of a wider accepted product
Ontology. The slice must cite its parent and preserve parent identity,
relationship, lifecycle, authority, and function law. Copying selected rows into
a new local model without that derivation creates another truth surface.

constraints.statement: The asset must cite one accepted Ontology and include/reference entity/relationship inventory, invariant/cardinality law, entity-lifecycle completeness matrix, authority matrix, atomic/higher-order function derivation matrix, applicable composition/effect algebra, whole-family Prime contraction with every accepted atom's admitted domain and realization mapping, and explicit deferred/excluded/unresolved functionality. A bounded slice must cite its accepted parent and preserve parent identity, relationship, lifecycle, authority and function law; copying rows without that derivation creates another truth surface.

conditions: A bounded action and accepted material-frame basis are assessed.

grounding.quote:
| preserves | Operates inside the intact relation. |
| changes | Alters the relation and requires acceptance by re-entry at that relation. |
| duplicates | Establishes an equivalent path explicitly disposed as constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realization. |
| violates | Contradicts the relation, leaves an equivalent path undisposed, or accepts a changed relation only inside the acting frame. |

constraints.statement: Contract application uses both selected STDO method relations/deciding laws and accepted design's concrete values; neither substitutes for the other and repeating method text is not reconstruction. Recover every governing relation in the causally closed affected set. Preserves operates within an intact relation; changes alters it with acceptance by re-entry there; duplicates establishes an equivalent path explicitly disposed as constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realization; violates contradicts a relation, leaves an equivalent path undisposed or accepts a change only inside the acting frame. Sufficiency is action/set-relative, not an extra artifact, universal future-change claim or reviewer-performance claim. Tests of boundary sufficiency use named cases with independently known relations/decisions, withholding conversation, commentary, prior-worker memory and implementation folklore as sources of missing relations.

conditions: Reconstruction sufficiency is assessed; lawfulness is a separate predicate when action conformance is assessed.

grounding.quote:
A proposed change or duplicate without decided acceptance/disposition retains
indeterminate lawfulness unless evidence already establishes a violation.
Unusable subject/basis and established scope/capability shortfall retain
invalid_basis and out_of_frame on the affected predicate. Preserve the action
classification, reason, performance and evidence; a label without its required
support establishes neither predicate.

constraints.statement: Complete demonstrated reconstruction satisfies sufficiency even when classification is violates; an established missing material relation or indistinguishable required case falsifies sufficiency, while unexamined support/undecided distinctions remain indeterminate. Supported preserves, accepted re-entry for changes, or required disposition for duplicates satisfies lawfulness; demonstrated violates falsifies it. A proposed change/duplicate with undecided acceptance/disposition remains indeterminate unless a violation is already established. Unusable subject/basis gives invalid_basis and established scope/capability shortfall gives out_of_frame on the affected predicate. Retain classification, reason, performance and evidence.

conditions: The active boundary is represented.
exceptions: Atomic function inputs/outputs are shown where they cross the boundary; higher-order composition is shown where it determines boundary shape.

grounding.quote:
The standard relationship expectations are:

- composition for owned subordinate payloads;
- association for downstream consumption; and
- inheritance only for real variant or outcome families.

constraints.statement: Show domain identity/cardinality rather than helper decomposition; ownership, invariants and lawful lifecycle relationships; applicable atomic/higher-order function relationships; IACS and Prime-atom mappings; subordinate and effect-edge-only payloads; downstream-only projections; deferred families outside the slice; authoritative/downstream roles; public/local visibility; composition, containment, association and real variants. Standard relationship expectations use composition for owned subordinate payloads, association for downstream consumption and inheritance only for real variant/outcome families.

exceptions: Participants may be explicitly external actors rather than domain-model members.

grounding.quote:
Every participant must exist in the domain model or be an explicitly external
actor. Every message must bind to a declared carrier transform, graph/C
constructor, interpreter action, or effect-handler call. A private loop,
service method, plugin, shell, or script may not silently replace a declared
workflow transition.

Every message must also bind to an Ontology function and its admitted authority
role. Actor identity or call reachability alone does not authorize a message.

constraints.statement: Show admitted input to result/truthful stop, naming owner and required authority at every decision, admission, execution, projection and effect boundary. Where applicable include malformed input/output, retries, recursion, fan-out/fan-in, nested workflow and human escalation. Every participant belongs to the domain model or is explicitly external. Every message binds both a declared carrier transform, graph/C constructor, interpreter action or effect-handler call and an Ontology function with admitted authority role. Private loops, methods, plugins, shells or scripts cannot silently replace declared transitions; identity/reachability alone does not authorize messages.
constraints.uncertainty: The cross-view section separately requires every sequence participant in the domain model; its treatment of explicitly external actors is unresolved.

grounding.quote:
Controller-local memory is not a lawful source of lifecycle truth when the
product declares replay, event, graph, or carrier ownership.

constraints.statement: Show the complete admitted lifecycle including refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation and terminal states the boundary can produce. Every transition binds an Ontology function and names its owning authority, admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act. When replay, event, graph or carrier ownership is declared, controller-local memory cannot supply lifecycle truth.

exceptions: Evidence/result records may be resolved by reference rather than duplicated.

grounding.quote:
Only supported applicability results determine exclusions. The conformance
gate retains those results as coverage evidence; it does not conjoin a true
exclusion's falsified applicability predicate as if it were a failed required
axiom. Unresolved applicability keeps coverage unresolved.

constraints.statement: Evaluate every applicable axiom. pass maps to satisfied on its exact evidenced predicate; fail maps to falsified with counterexample; supported not_applicable falsifies applicability under its owner law and gives no conformance judgment. Unsupported exclusion leaves applicability indeterminate and required coverage intact. Missing evidence, unusable basis and bound scope/capability shortfall retain indeterminate, invalid_basis and out_of_frame respectively. Preserve legal performance pairs, partial performed evaluations/counterexamples, never-undertaken not_performed and uncertain unconfirmed. Supported exclusions are coverage evidence, not failed required axioms. Minimum columns retain axiom/predicate, exact subject/basis, Ontology, authority, domain/sequence/state evidence, native and admission/compiler enforcement, original outcome, core verdict, performance/extent, effects and residual/gap owner. Bare labels are incomplete handoffs.

exceptions: Graph/compute visibility requirements apply to graph-native work.

grounding.quote:
For graph-native work, every batch, retry, recursion, or nested workflow must
be visible through the product's declared graph or compute algebra. A relied-on
`semantic_not_realized` constructor is a blocking gap. It may not be replaced
by imperative glue in a plugin, shell, service, script, or test harness.

constraints.statement: Prove every view element derives from accepted Ontology; every discovered functionality row is derived/deferred/excluded/gap; every sequence participant and lifecycle carrier exists in the domain model; every message has a declared semantic/effect boundary; every transition derives from admitted truth; every function/transition has explicit authority conserved through composition; public operations project Ontology functions rather than author peer semantics. Raw probabilistic output cannot directly become accepted/closed. Handler/plugin interiors require runtime ownership of admission, events, continuation and closure. Native types enforce locally decidable relations; admission/semantic compilation owns global references, completeness and realization gaps. Graph-native batches, retries, recursion and nesting must be visible in declared graph/compute algebra; relied-on semantic_not_realized constructors block and cannot be replaced with imperative glue.
constraints.uncertainty: External-participant consistency with the sequence model exception requires clarification.

exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor reuses accepted Ontology/design after identifying touched projections and proving no delta in entities, relationships, lifecycle, authority, functions, effects and public semantics.

grounding.quote:
For a new or semantically changed boundary, the Ontology and design decisions must
both be `accepted` before the affected implementation, public contract, or
semantic carrier is promoted or the work claims design-method closure. Any
failed applicable axiom, missing functionality disposition, unresolved
authority path, or blocking realization gap keeps the decision non-accepted.

constraints.statement: Apply Contract application to the exact assessment/support; conjoin required Ontology, views, constructability and axioms for conformance. Acceptance separately requires satisfied conformance and lawful mandate; non-acceptance preserves actual failure, unresolved or diagnostic results and is not itself falsification. Assess either decision's lawfulness separately with reason. View counts, empty sets and exclusions cannot replace coverage. New/changed boundaries require both Ontology and design accepted before implementation/public-contract/carrier promotion or closure. Failed applicable axioms, missing functionality dispositions, unresolved authority paths or blocking gaps keep non-acceptance. Assets must remain boundary-bounded; unrelated bootstrap, harness, projection or delivery shapes added merely to look complete are defects. Absence of Ontology, any view, cross-view evaluation or either acceptance decision means incomplete and blocks promotion, publication and closure.

conditions: Implementation precedes design acceptance or is under retrospective review.

grounding.quote:
Existing implementation placed under retrospective review may continue to
inform the affected design. Co-evolution remains lawful only while
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds; newly discovered material ambiguity,
contradiction, or materially non-equivalent network makes
`decision_complete(B)` false and activates the design gate for that decision.
Promotion and design-method closure remain blocked until the required
Ontology, three-view asset, and axiom evaluation are accepted. The design must
evaluate the code against prior authority; it must not rewrite the Ontology or
diagrams merely to rationalize an unlawful implementation shape.

constraints.statement: Only while co_evolution_admissible(B) holds may implementation precede/develop with design and be retained after reconciliation; until acceptance it is provisional evidence without semantic authorship, publication authority or promotion/closure standing. Otherwise only a disposable spike may cross the affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before acceptance. Retrospective code may inform design, but newly discovered material ambiguity, contradiction or non-equivalent network makes decision_complete(B) false and activates the affected gate. Required Ontology, views and axiom evaluation must be accepted before promotion/closure; design cannot rationalize unlawful code by rewriting Ontology/diagrams.
constraints.uncertainty: Full definitions of the two predicates are not included.

conditions: Material components, semantic boundaries, producer-consumer paths or algorithmic work are present.
exceptions: Software-module mechanics apply where software realizes the boundary; human steps need not be disguised as code.

grounding.quote:
A component may lawfully hold several roles. Three cases must be distinguished:
behavior already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new
operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are each
design changes. Only the latter two require re-entry. Use of a component
outside its declared role set must not silently establish identity, admission,
lifecycle, ordering, closure, or projection truth.

constraints.statement: Explicitly declare every material component's roles; technology capability grants no authority and composition/use preserves applicable authority. Existing abstract-role behavior is ordinary variation; new operational responsibility or semantic/authority role requires design re-entry. Out-of-role use cannot silently establish identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth. Prove computational/domain views describe one system. Machine, human and mixed realizations state operations, composition, effect locations, authority and material resource measures with units/observation boundaries; human operations retain input/outcome/refusal/recovery contracts. Material paths identify fact establishment, consumers, basis/invalidators, effects, alternatives and accumulated work, including material method/assurance operations. Component success and different names do not establish whole-path success or distinct responsibilities. Declare algorithmic input dimensions, workloads/growth and assumptions; bind Product-owned acceptance limits/authority before qualification, challenge representative paths/growth, observe work directly when timing cannot locate it without rerunning merely to count, and separate startup/framework/external/transport/assurance costs. No extra accounting system or fixed complexity is required.
constraints.uncertainty: UP-004, build-tenant binding, workspace reuse and UP-021 are referenced but not fully supplied.

exceptions: Independent implementations may be justified by isolation, substrate, performance, security or dependency ownership.

grounding.quote:
**Disposition is two-part.** Each material algorithmic obligation in `M(B)`
carries a *semantic disposition* — existing accepted relation, extension, or
new candidate relation — and a *realization disposition* — consume, implement
locally, optimize, adapt, or deliberately duplicate under stated non-semantic
constraints. Isolation, substrate, performance, security, and dependency
ownership are each lawful grounds for an independent implementation.

The invariant is not that equivalent code is never rebuilt. It is that a local
realization must not present an existing accepted semantic or authoritative
relation as newly owned local truth.

constraints.statement: Projection is subordinate and cannot adjudicate semantic identity, ownership or authority. Similarity yields a candidate, then semantic/operational equivalence evaluation, then reuse, parameterized common relation or justified separation. Compare identity/key law, ownership, ordering, mutation, consistency/concurrency, retention, failure, access policy, lifecycle and truth authority. Materially non-equivalent law requires separation; other differences justify it only if adaptation/parameterization weakens ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational constraints. Difference alone does not discharge Prime/recurrence review. Every material algorithmic obligation in M(B) requires semantic disposition (accepted relation/extension/new candidate) and realization disposition (consume/local implementation/optimize/adapt/deliberate duplication with stated non-semantic constraints). The law is false for materially equivalent algorithms/types without semantic disposition, generic machinery becoming authority, superficial commonization across differing laws, or local appropriation of existing accepted truth.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete definition of M(B) is outside this selection.

grounding.quote:
This is a theoretical justification, not an extra prerequisite.

The rules in this file remain engineering law even where the Markov-object
construct is irrelevant, unavailable, or still only candidate-class. The
theoretical framing sharpens the ask; it does not expand the scope of the
method.

constraints.statement: Engineering Ontology concerns one designed boundary; using the method does not require world-model adoption, Constraint-Emergence Ontology or other metaphysical/empirical acceptance. The theoretical analogy neither adds prerequisites nor expands scope; engineering rules remain applicable when the Markov construct is irrelevant, unavailable or candidate-class.

conditions: The method governs a realization boundary.

grounding.quote:
A good module boundary improves the likelihood of correct traversal because the
computation and evaluation surface is better constrained. This is true for any
intermediate traversal of the graph under finite context, attention, and time.
Review can ask what the bounded unit owns, what it consumes, what it emits, and
what proof is sufficient without re-reading the whole system.

That same constrained surface makes later consolidation into reusable libraries
easier. Repeated module-local computations are visible as recurrence candidates
instead of disappearing into broad orchestration code.

constraints.statement: Modules should be classified by the recommended roles. The purpose is a stable, bounded ownership/consumption/emission/proof surface for finite-context reasoning, review, maintenance and later consolidation, avoiding smeared semantic law across mixed authority surfaces; it is not a naming ceremony or a guarantee of correct traversal.

conditions: A new or materially changed realization boundary.
exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor cites accepted relations and proves no material semantic-boundary delta without recreating evidence.

grounding.quote:
- the final implementation must be traceable to the accepted Ontology;
- the final implementation must be traceable to design and module boundary
  assets
- unit tests must be traceable to module ownership, not only to helper layout
- implementation-first discoveries must be reconciled into the Ontology and
  three-view evidence before promotion or closure; and
- implementation may not compensate for an unrealized declared constructor by
  introducing a hidden controller or alternative authority path.

constraints.statement: Co-evolution may run derivation/feedback together only under its predicate; design owns structural HOW and false decision_complete(B) gates the smallest causally closed affected decision set before retained implementation. Final code must trace to accepted Ontology, design and module assets; tests trace to ownership; implementation discoveries reconcile into Ontology/views before promotion/closure; hidden controllers/authority paths cannot compensate for unrealized constructors. Implementation-discovered tests must re-express closure proof against ownership. Minimum chain is WHAT, accepted Ontology, target design, boundary assets/Ontology-derived IACS, accepted domain/sequence/state with axioms, implementation and tests from the same Ontology/boundary. With a reference, insert reference design and reference-to-target Ontology/design mappings. Skipping module reconstruction makes proof too weak. Module boundaries do not outrank constitutional truth/design. Agentic/probabilistic construction consumes SPEC_METHOD's execution protocol; this method supplies frame, admission, reconstruction, computational and module evidence, not a rival protocol.
constraints.uncertainty: The external agentic execution protocol and full co-evolution predicates are not supplied.

exceptions: Helper-level and transitional slice-gating tests may exist, but cannot replace module-derived proof.

grounding.quote:
Canonical rule:

- module-owned unit tests are authoritative for module proof
- broader integration, scenario, and sandbox lanes remain downstream proof
  families
- transitional slice-gating tests may exist, but they do not replace
  module-derived unit proof

If a module has code but no module-derived unit test lane, the module is not
closure-ready under this method.

constraints.statement: Tests must derive from module ownership, with accepted obligations as assertion sources and actual realization as executed subject, applying provenance and assertion/observation justification. Implementation-discovered tests must be justified/re-expressed against obligations before closure; existing proof carriers retain derivations/execution. Tests should trace to accepted Ontology/applicable laws, governing design, IACS/equivalent inventory, bounded views and owned requirements. They must not be authored primarily from helpers, private methods, incidental branches, temporary decomposition or mocks hiding the contract. Helper tests cannot become canonical module proof; module-owned lanes are authoritative, broader lanes downstream. Code without a module-derived unit lane is not closure-ready.

conditions: Every governed boundary, before design-method closure.
exceptions: Each lifecycle phase may instead be reasonedly not applicable or a named Gap:/Unanswered: with an owning follow-up.

grounding.quote:
If the lifecycle checklist exposes missing release, deployment, live-use,
telemetry, or retirement truth, the module may still proceed only when that gap
is explicitly governed. It may not close by relying on local convention,
implementation precedent, mutable runtime state, prompt prose, or test-only
fixture behavior.

constraints.statement: Evidence must state/reference upstream intent/requirement authority, realization, assurance/proof, release/package, deploy/install, live invocation, telemetry/projection/monitoring, retirement/revocation/supersession/decommission, and lifecycle decision owner/source truth/authority. Each phase is answered by an active owning surface, reasonedly inapplicable or an owned named gap; a bare phase list is not evidence. Code/tests/artifacts/fixtures can confirm a selected path only within owned authority and cannot invent lifecycle authority. Missing operational truth permits progress only with explicitly governed gaps; closure cannot rely on convention, precedent, mutable state, prompt prose or test-only fixtures.
constraints.uncertainty: Canonical phase definitions and gap-governance mechanics remain with unsupplied Spec/release clauses.

exceptions: Source truth's immutable-value preference allows materially necessary mutation.

grounding.quote:
Mutable carrier state requires explicit justification when it is:

- performance-critical
- required by the host runtime or framework
- modeling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth

Convenience is not sufficient justification.

constraints.statement: Source truth should use typed immutable values unless mutation is materially necessary. Mutable carrier state requires explicit justification when performance-critical, host-runtime/framework-required or modeling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth. Convenience is insufficient.

exceptions: Typed explicit failure is preferred where practical; totality is bounded by language and problem.

grounding.quote:
An unsupported/rejected domain label without its reason cannot choose among
these cases. Performance and effects remain separate core coordinates.
Closed handling does not promise external-computation termination.

constraints.statement: Bind function domain/result/permitted handling through Contract application and bounded construction. Prefer ingress rejection, admitted-carrier kernels, explicit typed failures, closed Result-like outcomes and explicit validation/unsupported/rejected cases; avoid hidden preconditions, semantic .get fallback chains and controller defaults reconstructing truth. Assessment binds the actual function predicate: established intended result satisfies it; rejection/nonfulfilment falsifies only when evidence defeats that predicate. Insufficiency is indeterminate, invalid basis invalid_basis, unsupported evaluation domain out_of_frame. A reasonless rejected/unsupported label cannot choose these; performance/effects remain separate and closed handling does not promise external termination.

grounding.quote:
Bind the actual write, publication, invocation or other effect boundary to the
core effect record through
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application).
[Workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) decides unknown
effect reconciliation and any dependent repeat on current owning state,
including after private context is discarded.

If a function both decides the semantic meaning and directly performs the write,
the design should be treated as suspect.

constraints.statement: Effects should be explicit/isolated; semantic kernels should not perform them while deciding law. A function deciding meaning and directly writing should be treated as suspect. Actual effects bind to the core effect record through Contract application; unknown-effect reconciliation and dependent repeat use the workspace/context owner and current owning state, including after private-context loss.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed reconciliation/repeat conditions are not supplied.

conditions: Each controller, manager, service, loop or public wrapper.

grounding.quote:
Apply [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application)
to each controller, manager, service, loop or public wrapper using its declared
role. Closure, identity, failure, next-work and current-truth determinations
must come from their admitted carriers, contracts or explicit design owners.
A wrapper that decides them through procedural orchestration, legacy fallbacks,
payload-fragment reconstruction or open-dictionary handling becomes an
undeclared semantic center and fails the authority/preservation conditions.

constraints.statement: Apply Contract application under the declared role. Closure, identity, failure, next work and current truth must derive from admitted carriers, contracts or explicit design owners. Procedural/fallback/fragment/open-dictionary reconstruction of those determinations fails authority and preservation conditions.

grounding.quote:
Coupling should be reduced by dependency shape, not only by file count.

Preferred dependency direction is:

`carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections`

Not:

`controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections`

constraints.statement: Reduce coupling through dependency shape, not merely file count. Prefer carriers → semantic kernels → effect shells → projections over controllers → service helpers → mutable runtime state → projections. Shared mutation, inferred/reconstructed source truth and duplicated semantic ownership indicate excessive coupling.

conditions: A boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor, executor, builder or substrate.
exceptions: Explicitly ratified strategy ownership permits prescription within that owned role and actual grant; explicitly owned assessment retains the assessment exception.

grounding.quote:
Where ratified responsibility explicitly includes strategy ownership, the
boundary may prescribe strategy within that owned role and its actual grant.
Explicitly owned assessment retains the assessment-boundary exception below.
This rule's additional domain policy is the governance/strategy publication
distinction and the listed lawful and unlawful forms. F2/F4/F6 explain its
authority boundary; they do not select governance-only responsibility for every
system or grant strategy or assessment ownership.

constraints.statement: Publish governance truth rather than imperative strategy law unless ratified responsibility explicitly owns strategy. Observation/route composition preserves actors' responsibility and grants; accurate information does not grant strategy. Unowned repair/action instructions, preferences disguised as observability, hidden prompt/report/read-model doctrine, and budgets/scores/counters/heuristics recreating another actor's judgment are strategy drift; the latter assessment is allowed only when explicitly owned. Governance-only systems cannot become replacement decision engines through context, projections, prompts or route helpers. F2/F4/F6 explain authority separation but do not impose governance-only roles universally or grant ownership.

conditions: Lawfully opened active boundary.

grounding.quote:
When a cross-boundary opportunity is discovered during lawful cleanup, it must
not be silently absorbed into the active boundary. It is repricing input. If
the owning authority admits follow-up implementation, that work enters
separately at the smallest lawful re-entry point.

constraints.statement: Cleanup is lawful only when boundary-local, behavior-preserving, authority-neutral, visibility-neutral without silent payload promotion and effect-neutral without hidden runtime/persistence/bootstrap expansion. Examples include removing local parser re-entry, consolidating local routes, improving local scans/algorithms and simplifying proof fixtures without changing module claims. Cross-module lookup/index/cache/persistence repricing, public carrier/visibility/truth changes, wider effects/observability or performance changes to Product expectations require explicit design re-entry. Cross-boundary discoveries cannot be silently absorbed; admitted follow-up enters separately at the smallest lawful point. TICKET_METHOD owns tracking/closure consequences. Improving an open area is recommended, not permission for unauthorized redesign.
constraints.uncertainty: Ticket follow-up mechanics are not supplied.

conditions: Repeated realization patterns across processed boundaries.
exceptions: A third local rebuild is conformant only when consuming an existing common surface, extending it before local implementation lands, or recording a reasoned do-not-commonize decision showing boundary specificity.

grounding.quote:
The rule of two is:

- the second credible recurrence forces a library/commonization review
- the third local rebuild is not acceptable by default

A third local rebuild is not design-method conformant unless one of these is
true:

- the active boundary consumes an existing reusable library/commonization surface
- the active boundary extends that surface before the local implementation lands
- review records an explicit do-not-commonize decision and why the pattern is
  still boundary-specific

constraints.statement: The second credible recurrence requires library/commonization review; the third local rebuild is nonconformant absent a listed exception. Prefer local cleanup, then tenant-local library, then separately re-entered shared/common propagation. Tenant-local authority-neutral patterns should be extracted rather than rebuilt. Changes to ownership, public carriers, module boundaries or shared/common law are separate design decisions. grounding.quote:
| `satisfied` | Admissible evidence establishes the predicate under its declared evaluation rule. |
| `falsified` | Admissible evidence establishes a counterexample or failure of that predicate. |
| `indeterminate` | The available admissible evidence does not decide the predicate. |
| `out_of_frame` | The predicate is outside the evaluation's bound scope or capability; it is not silently omitted from the wider obligation. |
| `invalid_basis` | The subject, governing basis or required interpretation is invalid for the claimed evaluation. |

Performance concerns whether the selected evaluation, separately from dispatch/admission/assessed work, occurred. performance fact or its uncertainty; it is not a fabricated child result. A
performed but undecidable evaluation differs from a known unperformed one and
from unconfirmed execution. A failed admission check can conclude while
downstream work does not. The plan fixes which predicates are required; a
precondition is evidence for its dependent evaluation unless the plan separately
requires that precondition as a predicate. A concluding basis/scope diagnosis
on P reports invalid_basis/out_of_frame on P with its supporting evidence; a
different admission predicate is not silently substituted for P. An aborted
procedure does not erase separately authenticated counterexamples observed
during the attempt. Every result projection preserves these
coordinates and the original predicate; a verdict alone is an insufficient
handoff where performance is material.

constraints.statement: Absent returns do not establish non-performance or undecidability: preserve absent required slots and known/uncertain performance, never fabricate child results. Admission may conclude while downstream work does not. The plan fixes required predicates; diagnoses remain on the actual predicate rather than substituting admission. Preserve authenticated counterexamples through aborts and all coordinates/original predicate through projection. References may carry results only with meaning/availability preserved; the core is not mandatory serialization or an extra carrier.

`not_requested` states an established effect-free scope under that operating
model; lack of a request alone is insufficient. A material possible unintended
effect without sufficient observation is `unknown`. If observation establishes
that an unrequested possible part did not begin, it contributes `not_requested`
at this boundary, retaining that observation and any earlier uncertainty.
It is not an uncompleted requested remainder. A requested part observed not to
